en.name: Gai lan
en.summary: Gai lan is the thick-stemmed Chinese brassica with broad blue-green leaves and small white buds, usually blanched and dressed with oyster sauce. No figure is published for it, so treat it like broccoli, its closest relative: about 4–7 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
en.pantry: Gai lan should not be left at room temperature. It is hardier than most Asian greens, but the leaves still wilt within hours in a warm kitchen and the buds open and yellow overnight. There is no room-temperature figure here and none should be assumed. Bag it unwashed and refrigerate it as soon as you get home.
en.fridge: Bag gai lan unwashed and keep it in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where about 4–7 days is the working limit — a figure borrowed from broccoli, its nearest relative with a published number. It is thicker-stemmed and hardier than choy sum or bok choy and genuinely does hold longer than either. Keep the leaves dry and loose; trapped moisture turns the leaf edges slimy. Trim and peel the woody stem base before cooking, not before storing.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline exists for gai lan, so we do not give one. It can be blanched for 2 minutes, chilled, drained and frozen airtight at −18 °C (0 °F), where food stays safe indefinitely — but the thick stem is what people buy gai lan for, and freezing softens it into something closer to a soup vegetable. If you have too much, cook it now and eat it cold the next day rather than freezing it.
en.thawing: If you have frozen blanched gai lan, add it to soups or a hot wok straight from frozen. Do not thaw it and expect to serve it as a plate of greens; the stems will be limp.
spoilage: White flowers opened out and the buds browning
Leaves yellowing, or slimy and darkened at the edges
Stems gone limp and hollow instead of snapping cleanly
A sour or strongly sulphurous smell in the bag
tips: Choose bunches with firm stems, unopened buds and no yellow leaves.
Peel the bottom few centimetres of the thickest stems — the outside is woody, the inside is sweet.
Split thick stems lengthways so they cook at the same rate as the leaves.
Blanch in salted water with a drop of oil, then dress with oyster sauce off the heat.

faq.q: How long does gai lan last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 4–7 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, bagged unwashed in the crisper. That figure is borrowed from broccoli; none is published for gai lan.
No timeline is published, so we do not give one. Blanched and frozen at −18 °C (0 °F) it works in soups, but the stem texture that makes it worth buying does not survive.

faq.q: Why is my gai lan bitter?
faq.a: Gai lan is naturally a little bitter, and older, thicker-stemmed bunches more so. Blanching in well-salted water and dressing it with oyster sauce is the standard way to balance it.

faq.q: Do you have to peel the stems?
faq.a: Only the bottom few centimetres of thick stems, where the outer layer is woody. The tender inside is the best part of the plant.

zh.name: 芥藍
zh.summary: 芥藍是莖粗、葉片寬厚呈藍綠色、頂端帶白色小花苞的中式十字花科蔬菜，最常見的吃法是汆燙後淋蠔油。它沒有公布的保存數據，可以比照最接近的青花菜來看：4°C 以下冷藏約 4～7 天。
zh.pantry: 芥藍不應該放室溫。它比多數亞洲葉菜強韌，但在溫暖的廚房裡葉子還是幾小時就萎，花苞也會一夜之間綻開泛黃。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。買回家請不清洗裝袋直接冷藏。
zh.fridge: 不清洗裝袋，放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，約 4～7 天是工作上限——這個數字是比照青花菜而來，那是它最接近、又有公布數字的親戚。芥藍莖粗、體質也比菜心和青江菜硬朗，確實比它們耐放。請保持葉片乾燥、不要壓實；積在裡面的水氣會讓葉緣變黏。粗硬的莖基請在烹調前才削，不要保存前就處理。
zh.freezer: 芥藍沒有冷凍保存期限，所以我們不提供數字。它可以汆燙 2 分鐘、冰鎮瀝乾後密封冷凍於 −18°C，在該溫度下安全上可無限期保存——但大家買芥藍要的就是那根粗莖，而冷凍會把它軟化成比較接近湯料的東西。真的太多的話，現在煮起來、隔天當冷菜吃，會比冷凍好。
zh.thawing: 如果是汆燙後冷凍的，請不解凍直接下湯或下熱鍋。不要解凍後還指望端出一盤青菜，莖一定是軟的。
spoilage: 白花綻開，花苞開始轉褐
葉片泛黃，或葉緣變黏、發暗
莖變軟中空，折起來不再清脆斷開
袋內有酸味或濃重的硫磺味
tips: 挑莖結實、花苞未開、沒有黃葉的。
粗莖底部幾公分削掉外層——外面是粗纖維，裡面很甜。
粗莖縱向剖開，才能和葉子同時熟。
用加鹽和一點油的滾水汆燙，離火後再淋蠔油。

faq.q: 芥藍放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、不清洗裝袋放蔬果室，約 4～7 天。這個數字是比照青花菜而來；芥藍本身沒有公布的數據。
沒有公布的期限，所以我們不給數字。汆燙後冷凍於 −18°C 可以拿來煮湯，但讓它值得買的莖部口感撐不過去。
芥藍本來就帶一點苦味，莖愈粗、愈老的更明顯。用足量鹽水汆燙再淋蠔油，是平衡它的標準做法。

faq.q: 芥藍的莖一定要削皮嗎？
faq.a: 只需要削粗莖底部那幾公分，外層纖維較老。裡面柔嫩的部分其實是整株最好吃的地方。
